title: Ireland's most haunted castle ranks among world's scariest Halloween spots
excerpt: Charleville Castle in Tullamore, Co Offaly, has been ranked No. 8 in the world's scariest Halloween locations, according to a global ranking based on TripAdvisor reviews — joining Salem and the Tower of London on the list.
content:
Charleville Castle in Tullamore, Co Offaly, has been ranked No. 8 in the world's scariest Halloween locations, according to a global ranking based on TripAdvisor reviews — joining Salem and the Tower of London on the list.

10:00 ET, 31 Oct 2026

Ireland's most haunted residence has secured a spot in a Top 10 ranking of the world's most terrifying Halloween destinations.

The eerie and gothic Charleville Castle has claimed the No. 8 position in a global list of the most spine-chilling places to stay, determined by analyzing TripAdvisor reviews.

The 225-year-old castle – situated near Tullamore in Co Offaly – is believed to be haunted by the spirit of a young girl named Harriet, the youngest daughter of the third Earl of Charleville. Harriet, 8, met a tragic end on the grand main staircase of the magnificent estate while sliding down the banisters in 1861.

Charleville Castle is so notoriously spooky that it has been featured on paranormal television programs such as Ghost Hunters International, and has been investigated by countless supernatural enthusiasts and psychics from across the globe.

The castle was designed by Francis Johnston, the same architect responsible for the historic General Post Office in Dublin. Now, Charleville Castle has earned its place among the globe's most haunted locations, alongside Salem and the Romanian site where Vlad the Impaler was imprisoned, as well as the eerie Tower of London, for those seeking a frightening getaway before Halloween.

Ballygally Castle, dating back to 1625, and Kinnitty Castle in Co. Kildare are one of the most haunted castles in Ireland along with Leap Castle in County Offaly.
